name: CA-38
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting seat has a D+8 partisan lean that points clearly toward Democrats
Hilda Solis has raised $1.4 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Pedro Casas shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near certain at roughly 98%
No public general-election polling or expert ratings exist for this race
model.rationale: The fundamentals, money gap, and market pricing all point the same way: this newly drawn Democratic-leaning seat is very likely to elect Solis, who has heavily outraised an underfunded Republican opponent. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on the seat's partisan lean and the absence of any evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any sign of Republican fundraising or outside spending, or polling showing the margin far tighter than the seat's lean, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 38th District is an open seat created by redistricting with a Democratic partisan lean of about eight points. Hilda Solis, a former congresswoman, Labor Secretary, and county supervisor, enters as the strong favorite with the name recognition and establishment ties typical of a front-runner. Pedro Casas, the Republican nominee, has no reported fundraising, cash on hand, or outside support.

The money gap is stark: Solis has raised roughly $1.4 million and faced no outside opposition spending. Prediction markets put her chances near 98 percent. No general-election polls or expert race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals, which align with her financial and profile advantages. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
